```{=html}
<section class="mint-landing">

  <div class="mint-hero">
    <p class="mint-eyebrow">Malaria intervention modelling</p>
    <h1 class="mint-wordmark">MINTverse</h1>
    <p class="mint-subtitle">
      MINTverse is two Python packages, estiMINT and stateMINT, the first estimating the EIR
      from a measured prevalence and the setting it was measured in, the second emulating the
      prevalence and case trajectories that follow a campaign. The emulator returns a
      trajectory in milliseconds, where the individual-based simulation it replaces takes
      minutes.
    </p>
    <div class="mint-actions">
      <a class="mint-btn mint-btn-primary" href="chapters/02-getting-started/index.html">Get started</a>
      <a class="mint-btn mint-btn-ghost" href="chapters/01-python/index.html">New to Python?</a>
      <a class="mint-btn mint-btn-ghost" href="https://github.com/CosmoNaught/MINTverse" target="_blank" rel="noopener">GitHub</a>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="mint-features">
    <div class="mint-card">
      <h3>estiMINT</h3>
      <p>Estimates the entomological inoculation rate (EIR) and the human biting rate (HBR) from a measured prevalence and the setting it was measured in. Both are single equilibrium values, not trajectories.</p>
    </div>
    <div class="mint-card">
      <h3>stateMINT</h3>
      <p>Emulates the individual-based model, returning under-5 prevalence and clinical cases over the three years before a campaign and the three years after, in milliseconds per scenario.</p>
    </div>
    <div class="mint-card">
      <h3>New to Python?</h3>
      <p>Readers coming from R, and meeting Python for the first time, should start with <a href="chapters/01-python/index.html">Python for Malaria Modellers</a>, which covers the interpreter, the environment, and the notebook from scratch.</p>
    </div>
  </div>

  <section class="mint-section" aria-labelledby="mint-install-heading">

    <pre class="mint-codeblock"><code>pip install estimint mintstate</code></pre>
```
